symbols.name: matrix P
symbols.meaning: A matrix whose entries $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ are indexed by its rows and columns.
symbols.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix with rows indexed by $\upsilon$ and columns indexed by $\varrho$, so $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\varrho$.

symbols.name: matrix Q
symbols.meaning: A second matrix whose entries $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ are indexed by its rows and columns.
symbols.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix with rows indexed by $\varpi$ and columns indexed by $\varsigma$, so $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ is its entry in row $\varpi$ and column $\varsigma$.

symbols.name: row index of P
symbols.meaning: The row index of the matrix $P$, running over its rows.
symbols.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix with rows indexed by $\upsilon$ and columns indexed by $\varrho$, so $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\varrho$.

symbols.name: column index of P
symbols.meaning: The column index of the matrix $P$, running over its columns.
symbols.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix with rows indexed by $\upsilon$ and columns indexed by $\varrho$, so $p_{\upsilon\varrho}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\varrho$.

symbols.name: row index of Q
symbols.meaning: The row index of the matrix $Q$, running over its rows.
symbols.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix with rows indexed by $\varpi$ and columns indexed by $\varsigma$, so $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ is its entry in row $\varpi$ and column $\varsigma$.

symbols.name: column index of Q
symbols.meaning: The column index of the matrix $Q$, running over its columns.
symbols.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix with rows indexed by $\varpi$ and columns indexed by $\varsigma$, so $q_{\varpi\varsigma}$ is its entry in row $\varpi$ and column $\varsigma$.

symbols.name: factor count
symbols.meaning: The number of factors of a tensor power, which is also the number of coordinates it acts on.
symbols.quote: The $\Upsilon$-fold tensor power, where $\Upsilon\ge 1$ is a count, the number of factors and of coordinates acted on, is defined by $P^{\otimes 1}=P$ and $P^{\otimes\Upsilon}=P\otimes P^{\otimes(\Upsilon-1)}$.

symbols.name: second matrix P'
symbols.meaning: A matrix of a size compatible with $P$, used in the mixed-product rule.
symbols.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

symbols.name: second matrix Q'
symbols.meaning: A matrix of a size compatible with $Q$, used in the mixed-product rule.
symbols.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

symbols.name: column index of P'
symbols.meaning: The column index of the matrix $P'$, running over its columns.
symbols.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

symbols.name: column index of Q'
symbols.meaning: The column index of the matrix $Q'$, running over its columns.
symbols.quote: For second matrices $P'$ and $Q'$ of compatible sizes, let $P'$ have rows indexed by $\varrho$ and columns indexed by $\vartheta$, so $p'_{\varrho\vartheta}$ is its entry in row $\varrho$ and column $\vartheta$, and let $Q'$ have rows indexed by $\varsigma$ and columns indexed by $\Psi$, so $q'_{\varsigma\Psi}$ is its entry in row $\varsigma$ and column $\Psi$.

symbols.name: coordinate position
symbols.meaning: The position of one of the $\Upsilon$ coordinates, numbered from 1 to $\Upsilon$.
symbols.quote: For a coordinate position $\phi$ with $1\le\phi\le\Upsilon$, let $P_{(\phi)}$ apply $P$ to coordinate $\phi$ and the identity to the others, so $P_{(\phi)}=I\otimes\cdots\otimes P\otimes\cdots\otimes I$ with $P$ in place $\phi$.

symbols.name: single-coordinate operator
symbols.meaning: The operator that applies $P$ to coordinate $\phi$ and the identity to the other coordinates.
symbols.quote: For a coordinate position $\phi$ with $1\le\phi\le\Upsilon$, let $P_{(\phi)}$ apply $P$ to coordinate $\phi$ and the identity to the others, so $P_{(\phi)}=I\otimes\cdots\otimes P\otimes\cdots\otimes I$ with $P$ in place $\phi$.

relations.quote: The tensor product is built from matrices, the basic objects of [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
The tensor product takes its one-coordinate factor from the [Butterfly](butterfly.md) map $H_0$, which replaces a pair of values by its half-sum and half-difference.
